record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.original_question: Does ZFC prove the existence of a non-metrizable countable dense homogeneous continuum?

evidence.quote: Problem 32 (Hernández–Hrušák–van Mill [43]). Is there a non-metrizable CDH continuum in ZFC?

artifact.self_contained_problem: A continuum is a connected compact Hausdorff space. A topological space $X$ is countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if for any two countable dense subsets $D_1, D_2 \subseteq X$ there exists a homeomorphism $h\colon X \to X$ with $h(D_1) = D_2$. Working in ZFC (without any additional set-theoretic assumptions such as CH, MA, or large-cardinal axioms), determine whether there exists a non-metrizable countable dense homogeneous continuum.
artifact.status_search_result: While ZFC examples of non-metrizable CDH compacta have been constructed (e.g., variants of the double arrow space via λ′-sets by Hernández-Gutiérrez, Hrušák, and van Mill), these examples are not connected. The specific question of whether ZFC proves the existence of a non-metrizable CDH continuum (a connected compact Hausdorff CDH space) appears to remain open in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Countable dense homogeneity and λ-sets
status_evidence.snippet: ZFC construction of non-metrizable CDH compacta via λ′-sets, variants of the double arrow space (not connected).
status_evidence.claim: Non-metrizable CDH compacta exist in ZFC, but the known examples are zero-dimensional/disconnected.

status_evidence.title: Countable dense homogeneity and topological groups
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on non-Polish CDH spaces does not provide a connected compact example.
status_evidence.claim: The continuum (connected) version of the problem is not resolved by recent constructions.
